core.title: Give each artifact one producing component; consumers reference its contract
core.given: A plan declares component interfaces with producing and consuming artifact entries
core.when: The planner adds or changes a producing or consuming entry for an artifact
core.then: Declare each artifact as produced by exactly one component, which generates (owns) its contract; every other component using the artifact declares it as consumed and references that existing contract instead of generating its own.
prefer: A producing entry names the artifact, its destination, and (optionally) the path of the contract it generates
A consuming entry uses the same artifact name, names the producing component, and (if given) repeats the producer's contract path
The contract path field is optional on every entry but recommended; newly added components should carry explicit contract references
avoid: Two components declaring the same artifact as produced (split ownership)
A consumer generating or redefining its own contract for an artifact another component produces
Consuming an artifact that no component produces (orphan)
unless: Any entry may omit the contract field (it is not required, for backward compatibility); existing components keep working with implicit contracts
core.why: Single-producer ownership with consumers referencing the same contract makes bidirectional producer/consumer coverage and orphan detection possible.
evidence: For every artifact, exactly one component lists it as produced; where that producing entry carries a contract path, it points to the generated contract (entries without the field remain valid implicit contracts)
Every consuming entry names its producing component; where both the consuming and the producing entry carry a contract path, the two paths are equal
Whether newly added components carry explicit contract fields is checked only as a recommendation; absence is reported as a recommendation gap, not a violation
verification: Producer and consumer are defined for the check: the producer is the component that declares the artifact in its producing entries and generates the contract; a consumer is a component that declares the artifact in its consuming entries and references the existing contract.

The contract field is optional (not required) but recommended: absence on any entry is never a violation — implicit contracts remain valid — and on newly added components it is at most a recommendation gap.
Contract-path equality is checked only where both the consuming and the producing entry carry a contract path; entries without the field are outside that check.

Single-producer-per-artifact, orphan and contract-path checks are cross-declaration checks over all plan interface declarations, not per-file checks; detecting entry-level changes requires a diff-level observer over those declarations.

values: plan artifact that declares component interfaces with producing/consuming artifact entries (concrete kinds from the profile)
component interface (the stack's local term via the profile)
a producing entry is added or changed
a consuming entry is added or changed
the contract field is added or removed on an interface entry
artifact declared as produced by more than one component
artifact consumed with no producing component (orphan)
consuming entry's contract path differs from the producing entry's contract path (when both are present)

fires: The planner adds a component that outputs an artifact and declares it as produced
The planner adds a consuming entry for an artifact produced by another component
The planner authors a new component interface and decides whether to include contract fields
doesNotFire: Edits to declaration fields unrelated to producing/consuming entries (e.g. descriptive text or wording of other plan artifacts)
Implementation code changes inside a component that do not touch its interface declaration
Contract schema content edits that do not change which component produces or consumes the artifact

profileRequirements.meaning: How producing and consuming artifact entries are declared (entry fields: artifact name, destination, producer reference, optional contract path), the stack's term for these interface declarations, and its name for the declaring unit.
profileRequirements.bunValue: produce[]/consume[] entries in product capability interface declarations; producer entry: artifact name, `to` destination, optional `contract` path it generates; consumer entry: same artifact name, `from` the producing product capability, optional `contract` path; stack terms: 'product capability', 'product capability interface'

neutralityNotes: The core says 'component' where ATDD-Bun says 'product capability' (a bounded slice of the product); that mapping and the stack's local terms travel in the proposed idiom.plan_syntax#plan_ownership_declaration profile key, because the closed vocabulary has no key for plan-level produce/consume declaration syntax. Field names (produce[], consume[], from, contract, to) are stack syntax and appear only in that profile value and in bun.json itself. The two project-specific source examples (verifier_detail[3]/[4]) have no neutral equivalent and stay bunOnly, since bun.json is the delivered reference example. The 'DESIRED OUTCOME wording' example in doesNotFire was generalized to 'wording of other plan artifacts' (DESIRED OUTCOME being a stack plan-artifact kind). 'No detector exists yet' is a Bun realization fact (the rewrite records implementation.type: none) and is carried only in bunOnly; core:verification states the generic cross-declaration check scope and the generic need for a diff-level observer, without asserting which observers a realization ships and without adding any interim enforcement (such as plan review) that bun.json does not require. The splitSuggestion (extracting the optional contract-field recommendation into its own rule) is realization bookkeeping, not carried into the core; the recommendation itself is fully preserved in prefer[2], unless[0] and verification, so the core is neither weaker nor stronger than bun.json.
